♡Family Today♡

Autumn starts tonight at 8:05. Scottsville marked the occasion with a new oven — five burners, a griddle down the middle, and the Halloween towels on the handle before the box was even in the recycling. Congratulations to the cooks. Sunny days all week from here.

A warning worth passing on. Scammers are now using A.I. to build shopping websites that look exactly like the real ones — same logo, same photos, same layout — and they are good enough to fool careful people. Three things give them away. The web address is almost right: a letter doubled, swapped or added, or an odd ending like .shop or -outlet.com where the real one is .com. Read it slowly before you type a card number. The price is too good: sixty or seventy percent off a brand that never discounts is the bait. They want an unusual payment: a real store takes a credit card; a fake one pushes Zelle, a wire, gift cards or crypto. When in doubt, close the tab and type the store's address yourself. Pay with a credit card, not a debit card, so the bank can claw it back.
Had a migraine? Say so in the group chat — the day and roughly when — and the paper will mark it on the Barograph. Enough entries and we will know what the glass does before one hits.

Outdoor window Good all day once the clouds thin by noon. After that the forecast is almost boring in the best way: sunny, high sixties, cool nights, not a drop of rain through Monday. That run of weather is exactly what sets the maple color, and it puts Saturday's Harvest Moon under a clear sky. Pollen Ragweed high.

🍂The Turning🍂

The next state report is tomorrow afternoon. Nights in the mid-forties, days in the high sixties and full sun is the recipe the maples wait for; tomorrow's numbers should be the first worth printing.
The reds come from sugar trapped in the leaf when nights turn cold and days stay bright — which is exactly this week. Peak in North Tonawanda is still about a month off.

Tonight Saturn rises in the east at 7:45. Jupiter comes up at 3:24 a.m. The equinox is tonight at 8:05, just after sunset — the Sun crosses the celestial equator heading south. From here until March the nights are longer than the days.
Aries
The Moon in Aquarius sextiles Saturn in your sign today, a steadying angle. Saturn has asked a lot of you this year. Today it gives a little of it back — a plan that works on the first try. Kaylani, Luka
Cancer
Mars in Cancer holds its sextile to the Sun on the Sun's last day in Virgo. Mars leaves your sign within the week. Whatever you have been building, today is a good day to finish a piece of it. Gregg
Leo
Mercury sextile Jupiter is just past exact and still strong. Jupiter sits in your sign until next summer. Good day for a phone call you have been meaning to make. Leah, Tommy
Virgo
The Sun leaves your sign tonight at 8:05, at twenty-nine degrees and change. That is the equinox. Your season ends at the exact moment day and night trade places. Fitting, for the sign that likes things balanced. Derek, Joanne
Scorpio
Venus in Scorpio squares Pluto for a fifth day, and the Sun trines Pluto today, which takes some of the edge off. The tension is still there; today you can use it rather than fight it. Ariel, Claire, Garret

The top of the range 30.30, up another tenth. This is the highest reading since the log began — a big, stable dome of high pressure parked over the region, which is why the week looks the way it does. The climb is slowing, and slow is the easy kind. No migraines reported after yesterday's jump.

Los Angeles 28, Giants 6 — which takes some of the embarrassment out of the paper's Super Bowl pick. The Rams are 1–1, and they host the Bills on a Monday night three weeks from now.

✶The National Wire✶

1

Networks Suspend White House Pool Coverage

After the president barred three outlets from the building, the five networks that share the TV pool stopped covering him jointly. CNN, MS NOW and Politico have sued.

2

The General Assembly Opens in New York

The 81st session opened yesterday at U.N. headquarters, with Iran, Gaza and the price of oil hanging over the week.

3

U.S. and China Set Up an A.I. Hotline

An “incident line” for artificial-intelligence emergencies, agreed ahead of the president's meeting with Xi Jinping. A.I. now sits alongside trade and security on the list of things the two countries formally talk about.

4

Arlington Arch Would Hold Drones and Snipers

The president says the triumphal arch planned near the national cemetery would double as a military complex. Veterans have sued to stop it.

North Tonawanda · Oliver Street Bids Open Today

At 2 p.m. at City Hall. Once a contractor is picked, the stretch from Sweeney to Thompson comes apart for new sidewalks, drainage and lighting.

2

Pet Owners · Wet Dog Food Recall

Fromm Family Foods is recalling nearly 6,000 cases of canned dog food, including its turkey paté, after possible metal contamination. Check the can before you open it.

★The Marquee★

1

A Bible Film Cracks the Top Ten

Daniel and the Fiery Furnace opened seventh at the box office over the weekend with no major studio behind it.

2

Paramount and Warner Bros. Keep Talking

The merger that would put CBS, CNN, HBO and a century of film under one roof is still the biggest deal in entertainment, and still being negotiated.

🏈The Gridiron🏈

Five Days to Sunday
Bills · the Chargers at Orchard Park, Sunday at one. Buffalo is 2–0 and a three-to-one favorite; Los Angeles lost to the Raiders on Sunday. Back to practice today after ten days off.
Jets · at Detroit, Sunday at one. The Lions are 1–1 after losing in Orchard Park last week and are favored by better than two to one. New York played Green Bay even for four quarters; the same effort with half the penalties is a real chance.
